title: Antarctica against Australia
hook: Antarctica sprawls across the bottom of a wall map. How big is it, really?

knows: that Antarctica looks huge at the bottom of Mercator maps
doesNotKnow: Antarctica's real size against a familiar land
that Mercator cannot show the poles

misconception: Antarctica is as huge as it looks on a Mercator map.
objective: The learner can say that Antarctica is under twice the area of Australia (about 1.6 to 1.8), and that Mercator exaggerates it.

claims.text: On this lesson's Mercator map, which stops at 85°S, Antarctica is drawn about 30 times the area of Australia.
claims.source: Builder's node check: d3-geo geoMercator, scale 320/(2 pi), equator 8 px from top, clipExtent to 320 x 168 (bottom edge at about 85 S): path.area ratio 29.93 on the kit's 1:110m data. The question rounds to 30 and the stage readout shows 29.9; both come from the same code.

claims.text: On the Equal Earth map, Antarctica is 1.6 times the area of Australia, wherever Australia is placed.
claims.source: Australia is moved to centroid 72 S. Builder's node check: geoEqualEarth path.area ratio 1.589; sphere areas 12.24 and 7.70 million km2 (ratio 1.589) from the kit's 1:110m shapes, radius 6,371.0088 km. Moving Australia uses the kit's moveToLatitude (rigid rotation on the sphere, area preserved; see mercator-greenland c10). Stage readout stays 1.6 when Australia is moved: to be confirmed in QA screenshots.

claims.text: Antarctica is under 2 times the area of Australia.
claims.source: 1.59 on the kit's data; 14.2 / 7.69 = 1.85 with published areas (c5). Both under 2.

claims.text: This map's coastline leaves out ice shelves.
claims.source: From the brief (cm-geography): the 1:110m outline excludes much of the ice shelf, which is why the kit's 12.24 million km2 is below published areas. Not independently checked by the builder.

claims.text: Published areas of about 14.2 and 7.69 million km2 for Antarctica and Australia give about 1.8.
claims.source: From memory, not re-checked: CIA World Factbook (Antarctica about 14.2 million km2; Australia 7.69 million km2). 14.2 / 7.69 = 1.85, shown as about 1.8 in the lesson.

claims.text: Mercator cannot show the pole, so the map stops at 85°S.
claims.source: The Mercator y coordinate grows without limit as latitude approaches 90 degrees (Snyder 1987, ch. 7). The lesson cuts at about 85 S by choice of the frame (c1).
Equal Earth is an equal-area projection (Savric, Patterson and Jenny 2018); already verified for mercator-greenland c6.

claims.text: Antarctica sprawls across the bottom of a wall map.
claims.source: Hook. A statement about how Antarctica looks on typical Mercator-style wall maps (many world wall maps use Mercator or similar). Needs a source or softer wording; from memory.

recall.question: In true area, about how many Australias fit in Antarctica?
recall.why: Antarctica is about 1.6 to 1.8 times Australia. Mercator draws it about 30 times larger and still has to stop short of the pole.
